title: Brand Impersonation: Review, Evidence & Reporting
description: Build an official account register, triage brand lookalikes, save an evidence packet and verify the outcome of a platform report.
intro: Brand impersonation monitoring starts with an inventory of accounts you control and a process for reviewing lookalikes. A similar handle alone is weak evidence. A useful review identifies copied branding, misleading contact details or payment instructions, saves a reproducible record and uses the platform reporting route.

sections.heading: Build the official baseline
sections.body:
List each official account URL, exact handle, account owner, and recovery contact in a private register, and publish the official links on your own website so customers have a reliable reference.

Record known regional accounts, resellers, and parody accounts separately because a handle containing your brand is not automatically an impersonator. If your team changes a handle, update both the website and register right away.

sections.heading: Search for variants with a bounded schedule
sections.body:
Use each platform search for the exact brand and plausible variants: punctuation changes, a doubled letter, support or help appended to the name, and the old handle after a rename. Search engines can supplement this with a query such as site:instagram.com "Example Studio", though results can be stale.

Example Studio is a fictional worked example. Prioritize channels where customers actually contact you, set a review interval and owner, and note that MyRecon is an on-demand public username check rather than a continuous alert service.

sections.heading: Triage copied branding and harmful behavior
sections.body:
For each candidate, note its exact URL, current handle, copied logo or description, any claim to be official, and the destination of visible links, then compare these with your official baseline.

Classify each case as a name collision, disclosed parody, unresolved lookalike, or documented impersonation concern. A copied logo paired with a payment request needs immediate reporting, whereas an empty handle does not; never contact or pay a suspected account to test it.

sections.heading: Preserve a small evidence packet
sections.body:
Save a screenshot that includes the handle, relevant claim, and visible URL alongside an observation timestamp and timezone. Keep the original page URL with it because a screenshot alone can lose context.

If the evidence comes from a customer, get permission to retain it and redact unrelated personal details. Keep a separate status for evidence unavailable behind a login screen; an inaccessible profile does not establish that an account is harmless or fake.

sections.heading: Report, notify and recheck
sections.body:
Use the platform impersonation form from its official help center, submit only the requested proof of authority, and save the report reference. If customers are at risk, publish a factual notice through verified channels listing your official contact and payment domains.

Avoid naming an unresolved candidate as a confirmed fraudster. Revisit the exact candidate URL after the platform responds and record removed, still accessible, or unable to verify.

sections.heading: Worked example: support lookalike
sections.body:
Suppose the official handle is example_studio and a candidate example_studio_help copies the logo and says payments must go through example-payments.invalid (a reserved placeholder domain, not a real destination).

The useful report contains both account URLs, the observed payment instruction, timestamped screenshots, and the official payment-domain reference. That documents an impersonation concern without identifying the operator; if the candidate only shares a display name, leave it unresolved.

cta.label: Search a public username with MyRecon

faq.question: Does MyRecon automatically watch my brand?
faq.answer: No. Use scheduled manual reviews or a separate alert service. MyRecon supplies on-demand public username leads on supported platforms.

faq.question: Should every similar username be reported?
faq.answer: No. Review the claim, branding and behavior first. Name collisions and clearly disclosed fan or parody accounts need context.

faq.question: Does submitting a report prove an account will be removed?
faq.answer: No. The platform decides. Save its response and recheck the original URL.

takeaways: Search for variants with a bounded schedule
Triage copied branding and harmful behavior
method: Worked examples are illustrative unless explicitly labeled as observed. Product limits were checked against the release source; linked provider instructions describe external workflows, not a claim that every account flow was tested.
